key_insight: Coarse-graining qualifies as generalized emergence only when an admissible, nontrivial functor improves a specified description attribute under a chosen comparison order.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a conceptual basis for assessing whether reduced engineering models improve selected structural or dynamical attributes rather than merely reduce complexity.
method: Represent system descriptions as categories and coarse-grainings as functors.
Separate structural admissibility from improvement in one or more chosen attributes.
For dynamical models, distinguish state and dynamical coarse-graining and link them through strict or approximate closure.
evidence_signal: Static polygon and network examples demonstrate symmetry and cohesion improvements, alongside equally coarse counterexamples that fail the emergence criterion.
watch_item: Results depend on the chosen attributes, comparison order, and admissible coarse-grainings; optimization guarantees neither uniqueness nor emergence.
paper_title: Generalized Emergence through Coarse-Graining: A Category-Theoretic Framework
